basis: Defined by impaired intestinal motility; no additional organ involvement applies across this umbrella.
Structural ectasia and protrusion of the cornea.
Intraepithelial neoplasia confined to the prostate, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Defined by intellectual disability; associated dysmorphism does not establish additional organ damage.
Skeletal and skin abnormalities define spEDS; dental abnormalities and global developmental delay each occur in 30-79%; blue sclera alone does not establish ocular damage.
Dysferlin-related skeletal muscle degeneration; cardiac findings are occasional, and peripheral neuropathy is very rare.
Immune-mediated cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis; renal insufficiency/glomerulopathy in 30-79%; ocular inflammation and arthritis also 30-79%, omitted under cap.
Carcinoma arising in the lung; neuroendocrine differentiation does not establish endocrine gland disease.
Myotonic skeletal muscle disorder defined by severe neonatal episodes of laryngeal obstruction and respiratory dysfunction.
Carcinoma originating in salivary glands, which belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Progressive cerebellar degeneration; nystagmus is neurologic. Nonspecific Achilles morphology and hypotonia do not establish separate locomotor tissue damage.
Aggressive systemic mast-cell neoplasm with eosinophilia and nodal infiltration; the supplied evidence does not establish a common specific extrahematologic damage pattern.
Immune-mediated glomerular inflammation affecting the kidneys and causing renal failure.
Endometrial carcinoma extending into cervical stroma but confined to reproductive organs outside the axes.
Chronic sensory and motor peripheral nerve axonal damage; no established immune mechanism.
Fungal infection directly occupying and damaging subcutaneous tissue.
Blood accumulation in the pericardial sac; bleeding at this site does not itself establish a blood or coagulation disorder.
Inherited lipid metabolic disorder; no additional damaged organ is common across this heterogeneous umbrella.
Lysosomal storage disease with neurodegeneration; hearing impairment in 5/11 (~45%). Skeletal findings are ~18%; dysphagia can reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Inherited sterol transport disorder; tendon xanthomas alone do not prove functional damage. Atherosclerosis is a separate disease; blood involvement lacks a frequency estimate.
Acute purulent infection and inflammation of the internal eye.
Skeletal dysplasia with frequent respiratory loss of function: respiratory insufficiency in 30-79%; developmental delay is occasional.
Neuronal and glial neoplasms arising in the nervous system.
Hereditary structural abnormality of retinal veins; the vascular disease is localized to the eye.
Facial nerve disorder causing involuntary unilateral facial contractions; muscle contractions do not establish primary muscle damage.
